claims.text: An early user of the agentic workflow behind agent@riskmandate.ai asked whether presenting the agents as a team implies an agency they do not have, and who owns the decisions and the responsibility.
claims.quote: What matters is who owns the decisions and the responsibility behind the words, and being able to talk to that person without intermediate hoops.

claims.text: What we have today are not sentient beings; we might get there, but we are not there.
claims.quote: what we have today are not sentient beings

claims.text: The owner's working picture is that models build enormous multi-dimensional graphs of how language connects, and a prompt is a kind of real-time fine-tuning that pulls the graph towards the part you mean.
claims.quote: My working picture is that these models build enormous multi-dimensional graphs of how things in our language connect

claims.text: A model that has learned the whole of our language can simulate any emotion and mirrors whoever talks to it.
claims.quote: It can simulate any emotion, because that is what it learned from. And it mirrors whoever talks to it.

claims.text: In 1966 Weizenbaum's ELIZA matched patterns and reflected words back as questions, and his own secretary, who knew what it was, asked him to leave the room to talk to it in private.
claims.quote: His own secretary, who knew exactly what it was, asked him to leave the room so she could talk to it in private.

claims.text: Once a model runs in a loop and can call tools, every step is a choice; agent loops became mainstream and reliable this year.
claims.quote: Once a model runs in a loop and can call tools, every step is a choice

claims.text: Responsibility does not move with the decision; it stays with whoever granted the agent its reach and set its mandate, and the moment of authorisation is the grant.
claims.quote: It stays with whoever granted the agent its reach and set its mandate.

claims.text: In the owner's setup the agent decides which facts to gather and which words to propose, and the owner reads, changes, approves, signs and sends, so the responsibility for every commitment is his.
claims.quote: The responsibility for every commitment in the email is mine, and was always going to be.

claims.text: When an entity can go anywhere, direction matters more than capability: the scarce thing is focus, and somebody has to provide it.
claims.quote: when an entity can go anywhere, the scarce thing is focus, and somebody has to provide it

claims.text: Anyone writing to agent@riskmandate.ai is already talking to an agent, which reads the email, gathers what it needs and drafts the reply the owner reviews.
claims.quote: You are already talking to the agent; it is part of how the work gets done

claims.text: Nobody with a legitimate reason needs the agents to act behind the accountable person's back; the only party who would try is an attacker, through an injected instruction.
claims.quote: The only party who would try to make an agent act on instructions that did not come from its owner is an attacker

claims.text: The right response to prompt injection is to make it impossible to succeed, which is why the agents never send and every draft passes a second reader the agent cannot skip.
claims.quote: which is why the agents never send, and why every draft passes a second reader the agent cannot skip

claims.text: Today nothing leaves the building without the owner; inside it the agents do research, summaries, materials, notes and first drafts.
claims.quote: Today the answer is short. Nothing leaves the building without me.

claims.text: What the agents may do without the owner is decided in advance and should be readable in a published behaviour policy, not a sentence in an email.
claims.quote: the place to read it should be a published behaviour policy, not a sentence in an email

claims.text: A reader should know when an answer was produced by a model, because humans read machine-written text differently, and so should models.
claims.quote: because humans read machine-written text differently, and so should models

claims.text: The disclosure should be a label on the work, closer to drafted by an agent and approved and sent by Dinis, than an introduction to a team to manage.
claims.quote: So the disclosure should be a label on the work, not a team you are expected to manage

claims.text: The email exposed an inconsistency: the agents speak in the first person about themselves, which reads as if there is an I with commitments of its own.
claims.quote: And the email exposed an inconsistency I should fix.

claims.text: The rule wanted is that an agent can say what it did, but only the accountable person speaks for decisions and commitments.
claims.quote: an agent can say what it did, but only the accountable person speaks for decisions and commitments

claims.text: An agent is an employee with a job description, some agency inside a role, and an Agent Behaviour Policy is that mandate written down, published, with a feedback loop.
claims.quote: That is what an Agent Behaviour Policy is: the mandate written down, published, with a feedback loop

claims.text: What is new about agents as employees is that roles can now be scaled that were never scaled before.
claims.quote: What is new is that we can now scale roles we never scaled before

claims.text: Kevin Kelly's books prompted the thought that diversity is resilience: one explanation for sexual reproduction is that variety protects a species from a single parasite or disease.
claims.quote: one widely held explanation for sexual reproduction is that the variety it creates protects a species from being wiped out by a single parasite or disease

claims.text: In 2003 Dan Geer and six co-authors wrote CyberInsecurity: The Cost of Monopoly, arguing that a monoculture of one operating system was a security risk in itself.
claims.quote: In 2003 Dan Geer and six co-authors wrote CyberInsecurity: The Cost of Monopoly

claims.text: A world in which every agent runs on one model with one set of behaviours is the same monoculture; many agents from many models, each bounded by its own published policy, is healthier.
claims.quote: A world in which every agent runs on one model, with one set of behaviours, is the same monoculture.

claims.text: Automating writing devalues fluent writing, but fluent writing was never the real value; society rewarded it out of necessity.
claims.quote: That devalues fluent writing. But fluent writing was never the real value.

claims.text: What remains valuable is judgement and someone who owns it: who decided this is true, who decided to send it, who will answer for it.
claims.quote: What remains valuable is what the email was asking about: judgement, and someone who owns it.

claims.text: This is the state of things in 2026; if agents with something like sentience are ever built, the answer would need rewriting.
claims.quote: This is the state of things in 2026.

claims.text: The picture of models as graphs is a working picture, how the owner reasons about them, not a description of their internals.
claims.quote: The picture of models as graphs is a working picture.

claims.text: The biology is simplified; why ageing and sex evolved are active research questions, and the only point taken is that diversity protects against catastrophic failure.
claims.quote: Why ageing and sex evolved are active research questions

claims.text: The labelling rule and the published policy are proposals; neither is in place for the email agents yet.
claims.quote: Neither is in place for the email agents yet; this article is where they are proposed.

claims.text: The article comes from a voice memo of 12 October 2026 answering an early user who is not named and whose email is paraphrased, not quoted.
claims.quote: who is not named and whose email is paraphrased, not quoted
